newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria says World Bank offers $260 mln loans.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria says World Bank offers $260 mln loans.

text.p: The Bulgarian government said on Wednesday a visiting World Bank mission had offered an aid package of three credits totalling at least $260 million this year to help the Balkan country out of its financial crisis.
A government statement said the aim of the programme was to secure essential imports of grain, medicines, vaccines and basic foodstuffs, and to support structural reforms.

The statement, issued after talks between interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski and visiting World Bank chief economist for Europe and Central Asia, Marcelo Selowsky, said the first loan of about $40 million would be for imports of essential goods, and Bulgaria could receive it in April.
The second was a social assistance credit of $50 to $80 million in two tranches, the first to be expected in June and the second by the end of the year.
The third credit, for financial reform and restructuring of enterprises, consisted of two loans totalling at least $170 million. The first disbursement is expected in June and the second in December.

The caretaker cabinet appointed three weeks ago has pledged to speed up privatisation, shut down loss-making state companies and liberalise prices and trade rules. It will remain in office until after general elections on April 19.
Negotiators from the International Monetary Fund started talks in Sofia last week on a funding agreement linked to implementation of a fixed exchange rate mechanism to help stabilise the economy.
The cabinet has said it hopes for a preliminary agreement with the Fund by the end of this week. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 8569
